description: A four-to-sixteen decoder: four gate inputs make a number, and the one output that matches it goes to 5V while the other fifteen stay at 0V

inputs.text: With a cable here the chosen output only changes on a rise above 1V at this jack; with nothing here it changes as soon as the gates do
Adds 8 to the number being decoded while it is above 1V
Adds 4 to the number being decoded while it is above 1V
Adds 2 to the number being decoded while it is above 1V
Adds 1 to the number being decoded while it is above 1V

outputs.text: 5V while none of the four gate inputs is above 1V, and 0V at any other time
5V while the gate inputs above 1V add to 1, which is the fourth gate input and no other, and 0V at any other time
5V while the gate inputs above 1V add to 2, which is the third gate input and no other, and 0V at any other time

notes: the numbers printed beside the outputs are a joke from the television sketch and say nothing about which output is chosen; they decode in reading order, the top left one being zero.
the input labels are part of the same joke; the four gate inputs are worth 8, 4, 2 and 1 from left to right.
with nothing patched the top left output is at 5V, because no gate input is above 1V and zero is the number that decodes to.
